articles.summary: Generating videos of a specific subject from a few reference images remains challenging when the camera reveals surfaces that are not visible in the input. articles.title: DTCA: Denoising Token Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models
articles.summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) generate text through iterative denoising, enabling bidirectional context modeling and parallel token refinement. Recent studies have applied reinforcement learning (RL) to DLMs and improved their reasoning performance. articles.summary: Data science agents can automate end-to-end machine learning workflows, yet they remain far from competitive on human leaderboards. articles.summary: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. articles.title: AlphaBet: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Event Forecasting Agents
articles.summary: Forecasting an unresolved event requires finding relevant evidence and deciding how strongly it supports each outcome. Yet outcome-based training of Large Language Model (LLM) forecasters often begins with preassembled evidence at a single prediction date, leaving evidence acquisition outside the learning loop. articles.summary: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant scattering has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models. articles.summary: Learning velocity fields directly in pixel space is difficult and slow. articles.title: What Outcome RL Buys: Finishing, Reliability, Rarely Reach
articles.summary: Outcome RL raises pass@1 but not pass@k at large k (Yue et al., 2025). But every pass@1 is scored under a token budget. Every recipe also trains under one. On physics and math problems at fixed token budgets, we compare the pass@1 of 20 released RL models (1.5B to 32B) with that of the thinking models they started from. We ask whether each pass@1 gain is changed behaviour or new knowledge. We divide each change in pass@1 into three parts. Finishing measures answering before the budget runs out.

articles.title: T-DIG: Text-Conditioned Diversity for Image Generation
articles.summary: Text-to-image (T2I) platforms typically return several images per prompt so users can explore different visual interpretations and choose one that matches their intent. articles.summary: Long-horizon LLM agents interact with their environments through complete assistant turns while generating each action token by token. We observe that critic values vary primarily across turns, motivating optimization anchored at turns with finer credit allocation among tokens. articles.title: The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data

articles.summary: Multimodal perception forms the foundation of multimodal intelligence. articles.summary: Discrete visual tokens represent vision in a discrete form analogous to language, offering a native interface for multimodal modeling under a shared next-token prediction objective. articles.summary: When an LLM group's discussion is compressed into a short memory for a final decision maker, what should the memory keep? Two natural heuristics keep the rarest claims or the claims relevant to the decision criteria. articles.summary: Diffusion video models produce striking clips, but they cannot reliably render an exact formula, a correct chart, a rule-consistent game or narration synchronized to on-screen events. A different route is emerging: multimodal agents that write code to render every frame and synthesize every sound. articles.title: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions

articles.summary: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Harnesses are often revised and judged by how an already trained model performs under them, which assumes that what the model learned under one harness carries over to the next. articles.summary: Safe household navigation requires robots to regulate clearance and speed according to what an obstacle is and how close it is, without unnecessary conservatism. Yet existing evaluations do not test whether semantic safety distinctions are reflected in continuous motion. articles.summary: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. articles.summary: Physical reasoning underpins how embodied systems understand and act in the physical world, yet vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable on questions about dynamics and physical causality. articles.summary: Despite rapid advances in large language models (LLMs), their deployment in the sports and health domain remains high-risk due to the absence of domain-specific evaluation benchmarks. articles.title: Learning and Reasoning with Geometry: How Generation Helps Spatial Understanding
articles.summary: Image and video generators can produce spatially consistent visual content, but how to use this capability to improve spatial understanding remains underexplored. articles.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are bottlenecked by loading routed-expert weights from memory during interactive decoding at small batch sizes. articles.summary: We introduce OvisOCR3, a 0.8B model for a broad range of OCR-related tasks. However, precisely expressing fine-grained spatial structures and temporal dynamics in natural language often leads to lengthy and potentially ambiguous descriptions. articles.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
articles.summary: Memory is increasingly used in long-horizon agents, yet the net value of building memory over direct retrieval from raw history remains largely unclear. articles.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. articles.summary: Omnimodal large language models (Omni-LLMs) are increasingly expected to assist users while observing continuous audiovisual streams. articles.summary: In long-term interactions with large language model (LLM) agents, users reveal habits through their choices and actions.
